newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends up on rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends up on rebound.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed up on Monday on a rebound following last Friday's correction, with travel sector shares performing strongly in the afternoon, brokers said.
The B index rose 0.715 points or 1.1 percent to 65.872 points, on volume of 18.8 million shares worth $8.8 million against $8.5 million last Friday.
Brokers said middle-priced Huangshan Tourism and China Travel led the afternoon increases, as the market expected them both to post good 1996 results.
Huangshan Tourism was the star, jumping $0.432 or 7.54 percent to $0.456 on volume of 593,000 shares.
Tourist agency China Travel also performed well in active trading, ending up $0.022 or 5.14 percent to $0.450 on volume of 1.2 million shares.
Brokers said most investors focused their buying on those stocks that are expected to post good results, which pushed the index up steadily.
"Selling has faded, given the fact that most B shares are still cheap compared with their A share counterparts," one broker said.
"Recent institutional support also helped to improve market sentiment," he added.
"Technical charts indicate the index is likely to test the 68-point resistance level," a second broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded with 26 up, eight flat and eight down.
Chlor Alkali was the most active share on institutional buying, rising $0.014 or 4.66 percent to $0.314 on volume of 1.6 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index was slightly up on cautious buying in the afternoon session, but a wait-and-see mood would continue in the short term, brokers said.
The index rose 5.196 points or 0.52 percent to 1000.698 points on volume of 414.6 million shares worth 3.9 billion yuan. The SSE 30 index gained 11.194 points or 0.44 percent to 2583.085 points.
Lanzhou Minbai was the star on talks of its good results, soaring 1.24 yuan or 10 percent to its limit-up of 13.62 yuan, on volume of 3.9 million shares.
